children: could face an investigation from the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) over claims that the two retail giants aren’t doing enough to ensure foreign-made products aren’t misidentified as “Made in the USA.”
Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-Wis.) and Senator Rick Scott (R-Fla.) are asking the FTC to investigate how Walmart’s Sparky and Amazon’s Alexa AI shopping chatbots verify products’ country of origin.
The letter to the FTC cites the findings from Columbia University’s Center for Law and Economy, which claims Sparky and Alexa hurt American manufacturers and deceive shoppers over country of origin.

have the technical capability to detect and flag “Made in USA” fraud, and that Amazon’s Alexa blocks answers to questions about “Made in USA” products while allowing equivalent questions about products that were “Made in China.” The study suggests these shortcomings allow third-party sellers on the platform to falsely claim merchandise was made in the U.S.
Moreover, the study found that both shopping chatbots describe the inaction as a business decision, not a technical limitation.
“Absent government intervention, agentic shopping tools can be and are used to [circumvent] settled consumer protection laws,” the Columbia study states.

“If Americans want to buy products made in America, Amazon and Walmart should be helping them, not giving away their business to foreign knockoffs,“ Senator Baldwin said in a statement cited by The Wall Street Journal.
Last year, the FTC wrote to both companies about third-party sellers falsely claiming their products were made in the U.S., in violation of the agency’s 2021 ”Made in USA” labeling rule.
